pass_summary: All 11 tasks are implemented, substantive and wired; I tried hard to break D1's single-primary-scoring property and could not — no non-primary source can reach `scoreRisk`, and D2's single-object form is genuinely normalised to a one-element list rather than accepted-and-ignored. Four should_fix items remain, the sharpest being a prose/implementation mismatch: `spec-plan` tells the agent to collect reach for "existing `Modify:` targets" while `plan_impact` enforces coverage keyed on on-disk existence regardless of verb, so an agent following the shipped instruction literally gets its payload rejected.

issues.title: spec-plan prose says `Modify:` targets; plan_impact enforces coverage on `exists` — an agent following it gets rejected
issues.description: `targets/claude-code/commands/spec-plan.md` and `targets/opencode/skills/spec-plan/SKILL.md` (Step 1.5.0, item 2 of the plan_impact block) instruct: "collect that data for the plan's existing `Modify:` targets and pass it in the `reach` parameter". But `src/analysis/plan-impact.ts:216-218` builds the coverage set as `claimed.filter(f => f.exists && isReachRelevantPath(f.path))` — every claimed TS file that exists on disk, whatever its verb — and `resolveReach`/`validateSource` then rejects the whole payload if the primary source misses even one. On this very plan, files declared `Create:` in one task already exist on disk and are therefore in `candidates`; an agent that scoped its collection to `Modify:` verbs would supply an incomplete map and be rejected. This is exactly the mismatch the plan's own Wave-2 outcome warned about ("Task 7 must key its rule on `exists`, not on `verb`") — Task 7 complied, but Task 9's prose, written two waves later, still speaks in verbs. The failure is graceful (the overlap section still renders, per plan-impact.ts:246-258) which is why it is not must_fix, but the reach half silently never works for anyone following the instruction.
issues.suggested_fix: In both `spec-plan` copies change "the plan's existing `Modify:` targets" to "every file the plan claims that already exists on disk, whatever verb the plan uses — `plan_impact` keys coverage on on-disk existence, not on the verb". Apply identically to both copies, regenerate `src/cli/__fixtures__/target-parity/` once, and add an assertion in `src/cli/plan-impact-prose.test.ts` pinning the phrase so it cannot drift back.

issues.title: `AgentReachSchema` is not `.strict()` — a mis-nested `primary` silently selects the wrong scoring source
issues.description: `src/analysis/reach.ts:166-232` builds `AgentReachSchema` as a plain `z.object(...)`, so zod strips unknown top-level keys. An agent that writes `{primary: true, sources: [moduleSource, symbolSource]}` — hoisting `primary` out of the entry, an easy mistake given the two documented shapes sit side by side in `mcp-servers.md` — has `primary` silently discarded. `selectPrimaryIndex` (reach-sources.ts:156-159) then falls through to index 0, and whichever source happened to be declared first produces the verdict. That is precisely the failure mode D1 exists to eliminate: the risk score for identical code becoming a function of declaration order. The refinement at reach.ts:217-220 correctly rejects *two* primaries but cannot see a `primary` that was already stripped. The plan records this as a deliberate follow-up ("Two more recorded but not actioned"), but it is a one-line change inside a file this plan already owns, and it is the one remaining path by which a non-primary source can determine the verdict.
issues.suggested_fix: Add `.strict()` to the `z.object({...})` in `src/analysis/reach.ts` before the `.refine()` chain (zod 4 keeps `.shape` intact, so `sync-graph-tools.test.ts`'s `Object.keys(AgentReachSchema.shape)` binding is unaffected). Add a test in `src/analysis/reach.test.ts` asserting that `{primary: true, sources: [...]}` is rejected rather than silently scored from `sources[0]`.

issues.title: `target-parity.test.ts`'s lsp-tools.md rationale claims casing is the only licensed divergence — it is not
issues.description: The new comment block added above `ccPath()` in `src/cli/target-parity.test.ts` states "The ONLY difference is the tool NAME's casing" and closes with "the casing is the only licensed divergence." The diff of `targets/*/rules/lsp-tools.md` shows at least one further legitimate divergence that survived Task 9: the Notes bullet reads "`ENABLE_LSP_TOOL: \"true\"` in settings.json and `vtsls` being installed" for Claude Code versus "a language server being configured (`typescript-language-server --stdio` in opencode.json)" for OpenCode. The plan's own Wave 5 section already calls this comment "now slightly understated". Because that comment is the sole written justification for keeping `lsp-tools.md` out of `IDENTICAL_RULES`, a maintainer who trusts it will try to force the availability note byte-identical and ship a wrong setup instruction to one of the two platforms — the same class of harm the comment was written to prevent.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend the comment in `src/cli/target-parity.test.ts` to enumerate both licensed divergences: (1) the tool name's casing (`LSP` vs `lsp`), and (2) the per-target LSP availability note in `## Notes` (`ENABLE_LSP_TOOL`/`vtsls` vs `typescript-language-server --stdio`). Keep the closing instruction that everything else must stay in lockstep.

issues.title: Shipped threshold rationale still presents reach as the HIGH determinant after Task 11 measured that it usually is not
issues.description: Task 11 measured that restoring `hasUnexpected` (Task 1) drives the HIGH rate to 45.5%-90% of real changesets, making the reach cutoffs "largely unreachable as a differentiator" because `scoreRisk` is `hasUnexpected || isHighReach(...)`. Deferring the `impact.ts` lever to its own spec is the right call — it is a semantics change in Task 8's file and would have been scope creep. But the deferral left two shipped surfaces stating the opposite emphasis. `src/analysis/reach.ts:79-112` was edited by Task 11 (comment-only) and now presents refreshed classification rates ("61.6% LOW / 12.1% MEDIUM / 26.3% HIGH over non-test source") as the live justification for the cutoffs, with no note that in production those bands are reached only after `hasUnexpected` has already declined to fire. The shipped `targets/*/rules/mcp-servers.md` likewise tells agents "the risk thresholds are share-based (HIGH at ≥25% of the module tree)" with no caveat. A reader who sees a HIGH will attribute it to reach. The measurement exists; it is simply not reflected anywhere a consumer looks.
issues.suggested_fix: Add two or three sentences to the threshold docblock in `src/analysis/reach.ts` (already a comment-only edit surface for Task 11, so no behaviour risk) recording that as of 2026-08-26 `hasUnexpected` fires on 45-90% of real changesets and therefore decides HIGH before reach is consulted, with a pointer to the follow-up. Optionally mirror one sentence into the `### Code-Graph Reach` section of both `mcp-servers.md` copies so an agent injecting reach knows what its numbers can and cannot move.

issues.title: `plan_impact` reach attribution lines merge visually into the unscored-files bullet list
issues.description: `src/analysis/plan-impact-report.ts:232` does `lines.push(...attribution)` with no preceding blank line. When `missing.length > 0` the immediately preceding push is `...listPaths(missing)` — a run of `- \`path\` (Task N)` bullets. `buildAttribution` (reach-sources.ts:239-261) also emits `- `-prefixed lines ("- Reach: agent-supplied — …", "- Reach source: …"), so in rendered markdown the attribution appears as further entries in the "does not exist on disk" list. `impact.ts` does not have this problem because its attribution is pushed into a different context. Cosmetic, but it degrades exactly the section D4 says must read distinctly.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/analysis/plan-impact-report.ts`, guard the final push: `if (attribution.length > 0) lines.push("", ...attribution);`. Add an assertion in `src/analysis/plan-impact.test.ts` that an attribution line is preceded by a blank line when the missing-files list is non-empty.

issues.title: The deterministic overlap half is lost if `buildImportGraph` throws
issues.description: `src/analysis/plan-impact.ts` computes `buildImportGraph(project)` at line 224 and only builds `overlapSection` at line 239, all inside the single `try` whose `catch` at line 281 replaces the entire report with an error string. The file docblock and the reach-rejection path (lines 246-258) both go to real trouble to guarantee the overlap half survives a bad injected source — but a filesystem or parse failure inside `buildImportGraph` discards it anyway, even though overlap detection provably needs no graph. Low likelihood, but it contradicts the stated invariant that the deterministic half "works when the project has no code-graph tooling at all".
issues.suggested_fix: Compute `const overlapSection = buildOverlapSection(tasks, detectWaveOverlaps(tasks));` immediately after `collectClaimed(tasks)` and before `buildImportGraph`, then wrap the graph-build + `resolveReach` + scoring in an inner try/catch that degrades the reach section to a one-line "reach could not be computed" while still emitting `header + overlapSection`.

issues.title: Prose tests pin the literal string `plan_impact(` instead of binding to the registered MCP tool name
issues.description: `src/cli/plan-impact-prose.test.ts:81` asserts `doc` contains `"plan_impact(project="` and `src/cli/sync-graph-tools.test.ts` asserts `` "`plan_impact(project=" ``. Both are string literals. Elsewhere in the same suite the authors correctly refused this pattern — `SCHEMA_FIELDS` is derived from `Object.keys(AgentReachSchema.shape)` precisely so a schema rename forces a prose update, with the failure message "must be updated in the same commit". The tool name has no such binding: renaming the MCP tool in `src/analysis/plan-impact.ts:187` would leave `src/mcp/server.test.ts` asserting the new name and both prose tests asserting the old one, all green, with every shipped instruction pointing at a tool that no longer exists. This is the strongest test suite in the diff and the assertions are otherwise real rather than tautological (the rung-ordering test asserts order, the LSP test asserts the target's own spelling AND the absence of the other's, and the vendor sweep guards against a vacuous walk) — this is the one remaining literal that a symmetric-but-wrong edit could outlive.
issues.suggested_fix: Export the tool name as a const from `src/analysis/plan-impact.ts` (e.g. `export const PLAN_IMPACT_TOOL = "plan_impact";`, used in the `server.tool(...)` call) and import it into both `src/cli/plan-impact-prose.test.ts` and `src/cli/sync-graph-tools.test.ts` in place of the literal.

truths.truth: (Wave 4 correction) Both runtimes require `filePath` and `line`/`character` on every LSP operation, including documentSymbol/workspaceSymbol.
truths.evidence: The fix is applied consistently and completely across all four affected docs — both `lsp-tools.md` copies and both `spec-implement` copies — and is pinned by `plan-impact-prose.test.ts:266`, which regex-extracts every `LSP({...})`/`lsp({...})` invocation, asserts `filePath:`/`line:`/`character:` are present, asserts the old `file:` is absent, and guards against a vacuous match with `expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. Handling of the false Assumption 1 is exemplary: the prose test docblock, the `target-parity.test.ts` comment and the plan all record that BOTH platforms ship an LSP tool, and no test or shipped file asserts the false claim; the `LSP`/`lsp` casing test asserts each target's own spelling AND the absence of the other's, which byte-parity could never express. Marked uncertain only because this reviewer's tooling was restricted to `git diff`/`git log` and could not independently re-run `strings(1)` against the Claude Code 2.1.205 / OpenCode 1.18.23 binaries to confirm the underlying parameter-schema claim. The docs are at least internally consistent and self-pinning; if `filePath` turns out to be optional for `workspaceSymbol` the docs over-constrain but do not break.
